key_insight: Variantscape uses large language models and traditional NLP to extract variant–treatment–cancer associations from oncology abstracts at scale.
clinical_relevance: The tool may support precision oncology evidence review and molecular tumour board preparation, but extracted associations are not treatment recommendations.
method: Screen biomedical abstracts for gene names.
Extract and standardise variants, cancer types, and therapeutic agents.
Use LLMs to verify associations against abstract text and build a literature-derived graph.
evidence_signal: Among 886,195 eligible abstracts, 37,895 (4.3%) mentioned all three entity types; LLM verification identified at least one association in 35,224 papers, yielding 44,644 verified graph edges.
watch_item: LLM verification against abstracts does not establish clinical validity; the abstract reports no independent expert-validation accuracy.
paper_title: Variantscape: Retrospective Study of Large Language Model-Based Extraction of Variant-Treatment-Cancer Associations from Published Oncology Abstracts
